body: See also https://www.tjvantoll.com/2012/07/10/default-browser-handling-of-the-css-text-transform-property/
So... what do we want for `button` and `select`?

According to the blog post linked above that’s where there is currently no interop. I don’t have an opinion.

CC @Manishearth, @Ms2ger
Being consistent across all form fields seems nicer, if we have the option.
Yeah, that's also what people decided for normalize.css.

I'd like to be uniform too. @annevk thoughts on changing Firefox's user-agent CSS?

Otherwise, we could add a non-normative suggestion for button and select.
Related to #1046.
@dbaron should probably decide on this for Gecko. Seems fine to me.

Three years later, and the situation originally described in that 2012 blog post hasn't changed:

           | `<select>` | `<button>`
-----------|------------|-----------
IE 11      | none       | inherit
IE 6       | none       | inherit
Edge 18    | none       | inherit
Edge 15    | none       | inherit
Chrome 74  | none       | none
Chrome 37  | none       | none
Safari 12  | none       | none
Safari 4   | none       | none
Firefox 67 | inherit    | inherit
Firefox 11 | inherit    | inherit

A quick look through some popular "CSS normalization" projects turns up `text-transform: none` in three different places: [normalize.css](https://github.com/necolas/normalize.css), [sanitize.css](https://github.com/csstools/sanitize.css), and [marx](https://github.com/mblode/marx).

@dbaron you've been nominated to weigh in on this from Gecko's perspective. Would you mind letting us know what you think of disabling `text-transform` for these elements?

I guess it seems fine to have `text-transform: none` on `button` and `select`.  In Gecko it was originally there for `input` and `textarea` so that what users typed in text inputs didn't get transformed (see [commit](https://github.com/mozilla/gecko-dev/commit/dde7681290965256b449f68b8ef5e78c013495e0) and [bug](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=150341)), but since `input` is so many things it was broader than that.  Given that breadth, it seems fine to extend to `button` and `select` if that helps compatibility.

Thanks, @dbaron!

- Spec patch: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/4672
- WPT tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/17152
- Firefox patch: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1556554

I strongly disagree with doing this for the `button` element. It is **not** a replaced element - it creates CSS boxes for its children and flows them according to CSS rules, so properties should inherit as usual. Resetting `text-transform` on `input` (including `type=button`) and `select` seems fine though.

Thanks, @MatsPalmgren; that's a convincing argument.

In light of that, we may want to limit the spec change, only adding `text-transform: none` to `<select>`. That would require a change to Firefox which both @dbaron and @MatsPalmgren support.

In the interest of consistency (and to fully recognize the merit of Mats' point), that would also mean changing Chromium and WebKit by *removing* `text-transform: none` from `<button>` elements. @tkent-google and @litherum: would you be in favor of such a change?
IMO, it's ok to remove `text-transform:none` from `<button>`.
@hober can you comment on whether this change (remove `text-transform:none` from `<button>` in the UA stylesheet) is OK for webkit?

Yes, indeed.

Firefox has `text-indent: 0` which matches what is currently in the [spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#form-controls), but also sets some other properties like `white-space`, `line-height`, `color`... 

https://dxr.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/source/layout/style/res/forms.css?rev=e56017a57ea7#632

Also, there are other non-replaced elements that reset some styles, such as `table` sets `text-indent: initial` [per spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#tables-2).

So I think the question is: do we want to minimize the properties for `button` (like Firefox), or take the shortest path to interop? I don't have a strong opinion, but since interop is the main motivation for this change, it would be bad to end up with 2 engines making changes and 1 engine still being different.

Test for text-transform and text-indent for all elements, to find which elements are reset in the UA stylesheet in different browser engines:

http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/7113

| Test case                               | Blink | Gecko | WebKit |
|-----------------------------------------|-------|-------|--------|
| text-transform  reset               |  button input select textarea     |   input textarea    |  button input select textarea keygen      |
| text-indent  reset               |  button input rt ruby select textarea     |  button input optgroup option select table textarea     |  button input rt ruby select textarea keygen      |

OK here's a test that tests more properties, but only outputs cases where the UA style is "initial"

http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/7115

Blink
```
log: letter-spacing: button input select textarea
log: word-spacing: button input select textarea
log: line-height: button input rt select textarea
log: text-transform: button input select textarea
log: text-indent: button input rt ruby select textarea
log: text-shadow: button input select textarea
log: color: dialog html input mark select textarea
log: text-align: input select textarea marquee
```
Gecko
```
log: color: button dialog input mark select textarea
log: line-height: button input optgroup option select textarea
log: text-indent: button input optgroup option select table textarea
log: text-shadow: button input select textarea
log: letter-spacing: input textarea
log: word-spacing: input textarea
log: text-transform: input textarea
log: text-align: input select textarea marquee
```
WebKit
```
log: font-family: a abbr address area article aside audio b base bdi bdo blockquote body br canvas caption cite col colgroup data datalist dd del details dfn dialog div dl dt em embed fieldset figcaption figure footer form h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 head header hgroup hr html i iframe img ins label legend li link main map mark menu meta meter nav noscript object ol optgroup option output p param picture progress q rp rt ruby s script section slot small source span strong style sub summary sup table tbody td template tfoot th thead time title tr track u ul var video wbr autonomous-custom-elements applet acronym bgsound dir frame frameset noframes isindex menuitem nextid noembed rb rtc strike basefont big blink center font marquee multicol nobr spacer
log: letter-spacing: button input select textarea keygen
log: word-spacing: button input select textarea keygen
log: text-transform: button input select textarea keygen
log: text-indent: button input rt ruby select textarea keygen
log: text-shadow: button input select textarea keygen
log: color: html input mark textarea keygen
log: text-align: input select textarea keygen marquee
```
(Not sure why WebKit gives that result for `font-family`... Edit: filed https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/4192 )

Changing things in the UA stylesheet comes with the risk of regressing rendering in existing Web content. Therefore, I would suggest taking the shortest path to interop, unless there is evidence that a different change is low risk or all implementers are on-board with the change.

(Let's ignore `keygen` for the purpose of this issue, on the assumption that it will be removed from WebKit eventually. https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=167018 )

(I will also ignore `rt` and `ruby` for now, as those have special behavior per https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby/ and I don't want to analyze how that interacts with UA styles right now.)

The shortest path to interop, for each property, I think is something like this:

(proposal)
```
letter-spacing: button input select textarea /* like Blink/WebKit */
word-spacing: button input select textarea /* like Blink/WebKit */
line-height: button input select textarea /* like Blink */
text-transform: button input select textarea /* like Blink/WebKit */
text-indent: button input select table textarea /* table is currently in the spec */
text-shadow: button input select textarea /* like Blink/Gecko/WebKit */
color: ?
text-align: input select textarea marquee /* like Blink/Gecko/WebKit */
```

Note that I was abut to send a patch doing the first of them initially for https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1481112 (https://hg.mozilla.org/try/rev/680ffd20b8c7de31479bf46dc522bebec8b24d05).

Both Gecko and EdgeHTML inherit `text-transform` by default for `<button>` which demonstrates that this is web-compatible. That said, I guess I can live with the suggested UA rules in the interest of standardizing something.

Thanks!
